text: This is what the Lord GOD showed me: a basket of summer fruit.

He asked, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the LORD said to me, "The end has come for my people Israel; I will never again pass them by." [Footnote: The Hebrew word for "summer fruit" (qayits) sounds like the word for "end" (qets).]

versions.text: He asked, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the LORD said to me, "The end has come for my people Israel; I will never again pass them by."
versions.explanation: The vision turns on a Hebrew sound-play between qayits (summer fruit) and qets (end), which is invisible in English. A brief footnote preserves the point of the vision without altering the readable text.

text: "On that day the songs of the palace will turn to wailing," declares the Lord GOD. "Corpses will be everywhere—flung out in silence." [Footnote: Or "the songs of the temple."]

versions.text: "On that day the songs of the palace will turn to wailing," declares the Lord GOD. "Corpses will be everywhere—flung out in silence."
versions.explanation: Hebrew heikhal can mean either "palace" or "temple"; given Amos's focus on the sanctuary worship at Bethel, a footnote noting the alternative is helpful to readers.

text: Hear this, you who trample the needy and do away with the poor of the land,
saying, "When will the New Moon be over, so we can sell grain? When will the Sabbath end, so we can open the wheat market—shrinking the measure, weighting the shekel, cheating with crooked scales,

versions.text: saying, "When will the New Moon be over, so we can sell grain? When will the Sabbath end, so we can open the wheat market—shrinking the measure, inflating the price, cheating with rigged scales,
versions.explanation: "Inflating the price" loses the concrete image: the merchants use an undersized ephah (grain measure) and an oversized shekel weight for the silver. Keeping the shekel weight makes the fraud clear and parallels the following mention of scales.

text: buying the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and selling the sweepings with the wheat?"
The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob: "I will never forget a single thing they have done.
"Will not the land tremble for this, and everyone who lives in it mourn? The whole land will rise like the Nile, heave up and sink again like the river of Egypt."

versions.text: Will not the land tremble for this, and everyone who lives in it mourn? The whole land will rise like the Nile, heave up and sink again like the river of Egypt."
versions.explanation: The divine speech opened in verse 7 continues here and is closed at the end of this verse, but no opening quotation mark begins the continued quotation. Adding an opening quote at the start of the verse keeps the punctuation consistent for readers and lectors.

text: "On that day," declares the Lord GOD, "I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.

I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into laments. I will put sackcloth on every waist and shave every head. I will make it like mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.
The days are coming," declares the Lord GOD, "when I will send a famine on the land—not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD.
People will stagger from sea to sea and wander from north to east, searching for the word of the LORD, but they will not find it.
On that day the beautiful young women and the young men will faint from thirst—
those who swear by the guilt of Samaria, saying, 'As surely as your god lives, Dan,' and, 'As surely as the way of Beersheba lives.' They will fall, never to rise again."
